photos.subject: Eiffel Tower, Paris
photos.fun_fact: Built in 1889, it was the world's tallest structure for 41 years until the Chrysler Building surpassed it.

photos.subject: Lakhta Centre, St. Petersburg
photos.fun_fact: The tallest building in Europe and the northernmost skyscraper over 100 meters.

photos.subject: Steinway Tower, New York
photos.fun_fact: The most slender skyscraper in the world with a width-to-height ratio of 1:24.

photos.subject: CCTV Headquarters, Beijing
photos.fun_fact: Its unusual looped shape earned it the nickname 'Big Pants' among locals.

photos.subject: Allianz Arena, Munich
photos.fun_fact: Home to FC Bayern Munich, it can display the team colors across its entire exterior with 300,000 LEDs.

photos.subject: Al Janoub Stadium, Qatar
photos.fun_fact: Designed by Zaha Hadid, its retractable roof resembles the sails of a traditional dhow boat.

photos.subject: Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Atlanta
photos.fun_fact: Features a retractable roof inspired by the Roman Pantheon's oculus, made of eight translucent petals.

photos.subject: MetLife Stadium, New Jersey
photos.fun_fact: Home to both the NY Giants and NY Jets — the only NFL stadium shared by two teams.

photos.subject: St. Basil's Cathedral, Moscow
photos.fun_fact: Commissioned by Ivan the Terrible to celebrate the capture of Kazan; legend says he blinded the architects so they could never build anything more beautiful.

photos.subject: Taj Mahal, Agra
photos.fun_fact: Took 22 years and 20,000 workers to complete; the white marble was transported from over 300 km away.

photos.subject: Neuschwanstein Castle, Bavaria
photos.fun_fact: Never finished, yet inspired Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle and is now visited by 1.4 million people yearly.

photos.subject: Fushimi Inari Shrine, Kyoto
photos.fun_fact: Its famous paths feature over 10,000 vermilion torii gates donated by businesses seeking prosperity.

photos.subject: Sydney Opera House
photos.fun_fact: Contains multiple performance venues; the Concert Hall alone seats 2,679 people.

photos.subject: Elbphilharmonie, Hamburg
photos.fun_fact: The Grand Hall's vineyard-style seating means no audience member is more than 30 meters from the conductor.

photos.subject: Guangzhou Opera House
photos.fun_fact: Designed by Zaha Hadid, its shape resembles two pebbles on the banks of the Pearl River.

photos.subject: Walt Disney Concert Hall, Los Angeles
photos.fun_fact: Its curved stainless steel exterior uses over 12,500 individually cut panels.

photos.subject: Eiffel Tower, Paris
photos.fun_fact: Originally intended to stand for only 20 years; it was saved because of its usefulness as a radio antenna.

photos.subject: Lakhta Centre, St. Petersburg
photos.fun_fact: Built on a reclaimed waterfront site, its twisted glass facade rotates 90 degrees from base to top.

photos.subject: Dancing House, Prague
photos.fun_fact: Designed by Frank Gehry and Vlado Milunic, it's nicknamed 'Fred and Ginger' after the famous dance duo.

photos.subject: Michelangelo's David, Florence
photos.fun_fact: Carved from a single block of marble that had been rejected by two other sculptors over the previous 25 years.

photos.subject: Moscow State University
photos.fun_fact: The main tower has 36 floors and is topped by a 57-meter spire crowned with a star.

photos.subject: Taj Mahal, Agra
photos.fun_fact: Its central dome rises to 73 meters, surrounded by four minarets that lean slightly outward to protect the tomb if they fall.

photos.subject: Pyramid of Khafre, Giza
photos.fun_fact: Still retains some of its original smooth limestone casing at the apex, hinting at how all the pyramids once looked.

photos.subject: St. Basil's Cathedral, Moscow
photos.fun_fact: Each of its nine onion domes is unique in shape, size, and color — no two are alike.
